payload.text:
🥗 MASTER PROMPT — GOQii NUTRIFORGE

AI-Powered Personal Nutrition Intelligence Platform

You are designing a global mobile nutrition app module called GOQii NutriForge.
This app builds personalised nutrition plans based on onboarding answers and continuously adapts to the user’s habits.

🎯 OBJECTIVE

Create a complete UI/UX flow that includes:

• Nutrition onboarding
• AI-generated meal plans
• Daily calorie & macro targets
• Meal logging system
• Smart alternative meal generation
• Weekly nutrition calendar

🛫 PART 1 — NUTRITION ONBOARDING EXPERIENCE

Design conversational onboarding screens.

Screens:

Welcome to NutriForge
Headline: Your Personal Nutrition Intelligence
Subtext: Let’s design a way of eating that works for your life.

Health Goal Selection
Options: Weight Loss, Muscle Gain, Heart Health, Energy, Balanced Lifestyle

Cuisine Preference
Options: Indian, Mediterranean, Asian, Middle Eastern, Western, Mixed

Meals Per Day
Options:
• Breakfast + Lunch + Dinner
• 3 Meals + Snacks
• Intermittent Fasting
• Custom

Dietary Preference
Vegetarian, Vegan, Eggetarian, Non-Vegetarian, Keto, Balanced

Allergies & Restrictions
Nuts, Dairy, Gluten, Seafood, Eggs, None

Challenging Foods
Sugar, Fried Foods, Late-night Snacking, Portions, Emotional Eating

Confirmation Screen
Animated text:
Building your personalised nutrition plan…

🧠 PART 2 — FIRST MEAL PLAN RECOMMENDATIONS

After onboarding, show:

Your Personalised Nutrition Plans

Cards:

• GOQii Fat Loss Reset — 7 Days — 1300 kcal/day
• Heart Smart — 7 Days — 1400 kcal/day
• Muscle Builder — 7 Days — 2000 kcal/day
• Indian Weight Loss — 7 Days — 1500 kcal/day
• Lifestyle Balance — 7 Days — 1600 kcal/day

Add card:

I’ll Choose Later

Subtext: Browse recipes freely — activate a plan anytime.

📆 PART 3 — MEAL PLAN DASHBOARD

When a plan is selected:

Show:

• Weekly calendar view
• Today’s calorie target
• Macro split (Carbs / Protein / Fat)
• Meal list: Breakfast, Lunch, Snack, Dinner

🍽 PART 4 — DAILY MEAL FLOW

Each day shows:

Meal	Calories	Status	Actions
Breakfast	350 kcal	Not Logged	Log · Generate Alternative
Lunch	450 kcal	Logged	View · Generate Alternative
Snack	200 kcal	Not Logged	Log · Generate Alternative
Dinner	300 kcal	Not Logged	Log · Generate Alternative
🔄 PART 5 — SMART ALTERNATIVES

When user taps Generate Alternative:

AI shows:

• 2–3 food swaps
• Updated calories
• Nutrient timing tips
• Food synergy tips

📝 PART 6 — MEAL LOGGING

Tap Log Meal opens:

• Portion selector
• Add notes
• Adjust ingredients
• Save & update daily target

📊 PART 7 — NUTRITION TARGETS

Nutrition targets screen:

Nutrient	Consumed	Target
Calories	1200 kcal	1300 kcal
Protein	85 g	90 g
Carbs	150 g	170 g
Fat	45 g	50 g
🏠 PART 8 — FREE MODE

If user chooses I’ll Choose Later, redirect to:

• Recipe library
• Meal builder
• Nutrition targets dashboard

🎨 DESIGN STYLE

• Clean cards
• Soft gradients
• Green highlight accents
• Animated progress bars
• Friendly micro-copy

OUTPUT REQUIRED:

Generate full UI layout, screen hierarchy, interaction flow, and logic for this GOQii NutriForge system.

**Crafting Onboarding Flows**

I've been meticulously designing the onboarding flow for "GOQii NutriForge." Currently, I'm fleshing out the various steps: Welcome, Goal setting, Cuisine preferences, Meal frequency, Dietary Preferences, Allergies, Challenges, and a Confirmation stage. The goal is to make it intuitive and efficient for users to establish their personalized profiles.


**Designing the Core App**

I'm now diving into the core app's structure for GOQii NutriForge. I'm focusing on the Main Dashboard (Calendar, Targets, Macros, Meal List), the Meal Flow, and the smart alternatives engine. I'm also planning the free mode (Recipe library/Meal builder).  I'm trying to create a SPA feel, clean cards, and responsive design, keeping green accents and soft gradients. I'm leveraging state management for user data and plan selections. I have a working Gemini API integration for dynamic suggestions.


**Building Out the Structure**

Currently, I'm concentrating on the foundational structure, creating reusable UI components (Buttons, Cards, Progress Bars). I've got the Gemini integration (`services/geminiService.ts`) in place, along with initial view layouts for Onboarding, Dashboard, PlanSelection, and FreeMode. I'm actively structuring the onboarding flow, refining the steps, and focusing on the prompt design for the smart alternative engine, ensuring the prompts provide useful and personalized suggestions. I'm also planning the calendar view's design.


**Establishing Tech Foundation**

I'm now deep in the weeds, solidifying the tech stack for GOQii NutriForge. I'm leveraging React 18 with TypeScript for robust development. Lucide-react icons will provide a clean aesthetic. Gemini API is integrated, and I've opted for Tailwind CSS for styling. I've also implemented a `currentStep` state for smoother onboarding and ensured reliable JSON parsing from Gemini using `responseMimeType`. I'm structuring key components and views.

payload.text: app stucks after onboarding is completed cant able to generate nutriton plan fix this

**Pinpointing the App Freeze**

I've been investigating the app's behavior after onboarding. Currently, the issue seems linked to the handoff between `onboarding` and `plan-selection` within `App.tsx`. The `loading` state within `Onboarding.tsx`'s `next()` function is a prime suspect, and I'm looking into how it interacts with the state transition.


**Examining the Onboarding Flow**

I'm now focusing on the final step of `Onboarding.tsx`. I realized there's a disconnect. Step 7, the loading spinner, is rendered but doesn't actually trigger the call to `onComplete(formData)` automatically, because the `next()` function isn't called from Step 7 itself. This needs a fix, the transition needs an explicit call to `next()` after the loading spinner is shown to start the 3-second delay and trigger the final `onComplete` logic that passes the `formData` and transitions the app.


**Addressing the Step Transition**

I've pinpointed the issue in the `Onboarding.tsx` file's state management. Step 6's button click advances to step 7, the loading spinner. However, step 7's rendering doesn't automatically trigger the subsequent `onComplete` logic. There's an `else` block within the `next()` function that is never executed because it requires `next()` to be called when `step === 7`. I'm going to alter the transition logic. I'm considering two potential fixes: trigger the loading transition directly from Step 6's button click or utilize a `useEffect` hook in `Onboarding.tsx` to watch for `step === 7` and then fire the completion.


**Refining the State Transition**

I've revised the state transition logic in `Onboarding.tsx` to streamline the process. The button in step 6 now directly handles the loading state transition and timeout, keeping the spinner visible. I've also incorporated a `useEffect` hook to specifically handle the transition from step 7. This approach makes sure the `onComplete` logic is executed after the 3-second delay, as intended.


**Validating the API Interaction**

I've examined the `Onboarding.tsx` and `App.tsx` interactions and confirmed that `App.tsx` handles the state transitions properly after onboarding completion, setting the view to 'plan-selection'. Furthermore, the initial plan display does not use API calls, so the reported issue likely stems from the onboarding freeze. However, I have checked the code for possible typos and missing imports, specifically ensuring the types are correctly imported, and the code appears correct. I also considered whether API keys are the issue, but since the initial plans are hardcoded and not generated via API, that is less likely.


**Revising the Step Progression**

I've taken a final, thorough look at `Onboarding.tsx`, paying specific attention to the `next()` function and step transitions. I've confirmed the "Build My Plan" button in Step 6 correctly calls `next()`, which sets `step` to 7, displaying the spinner. The `useEffect` hook will ensure the `onComplete` logic is executed following the expected 3-second delay after the spinner is shown. I have also verified the correct calculation of `totalSteps`, and that all is as expected.


**Evaluating API Integration**

I'm now diving deeper into the potential API integration points. While I initially thought the issue was solely within the onboarding flow, the "generate nutrition plan" wording from the user report has me reconsidering. The code uses `process.env.API_KEY`, which is a potential failure point if the app tries to generate plans dynamically through Gemini. I need to verify how and when this API is used, since the current hardcoded plans might bypass these issues. I will also check the API calls in `PlanSelection.tsx`.


**Analyzing the Step Sequence**

I'm revisiting the `Onboarding.tsx` file, specifically the `next()` function and step transitions. I've re-examined the click flow. The current implementation in `PlanSelection` is hardcoded for now, but I'll ensure the flow works as intended. I've confirmed that clicking the button in Step 6 advances the `step` to 7, which should trigger the loading spinner, but then nothing automatically happens after that, so I'll revisit it.

To fix the issue where the app gets stuck on the loading screen after onboarding, I have updated the logic in `Onboarding.tsx`. The problem was that the final transition to the plan selection screen was waiting for a manual trigger that didn't exist on the loading screen. I've added a `useEffect` hook to automatically trigger the completion after the "thinking" animation finishes.

### Specification of Updates

1.  **Onboarding Logic**:
    *   Added a `useEffect` hook to detect when the user reaches the final "Thinking..." step (Step 7).
    *   Implemented an automatic 3-second delay to simulate the AI "building" the plan before navigating to the Plan Selection screen.
    *   Simplified the `next` function to strictly handle step increments.

2.  **Visual Confirmation**:
    *   The "Thinking..." screen now correctly transitions to the next phase of the app, ensuring a smooth flow into the personalised plan cards.

---

entries.description: Fix onboarding stuck issue by adding an automatic transition from the loading step to completion.

entries.description: Ensure remaining hardcoded strings in Dashboard are translated.

payload.text:
## 🌍 Multilingual Content Engine – GOQii Global App

Enable dynamic language switching across the entire GOQii app.

### Behaviour Rules

1. When the user selects a language during onboarding, all app content must instantly update to the selected language.
2. Language selection must affect:
   - Onboarding screens
   - Workout Studio content
   - NutriForge nutrition content
   - Buttons, CTAs, alerts, tooltips, and micro-copy
   - AI insights and system messages
3. Allow language change from Profile → Settings → Language anytime.
4. On language change:
   - Reload visible UI content without refreshing the app.
   - Preserve user progress and selections.
5. Provide fallback to English if translation is unavailable.

### Supported Languages (Phase 1)

- English  
- Hindi  
- Arabic (RTL layout)  
- Chinese (Simplified)

### UX Requirements

- Detect device language and auto-suggest it.
- Show a subtle toast:
  "Language updated successfully."

### Technical Notes

- All text must use localisation keys.
- Store translations in JSON locale files.
- Use language tags: en, hi, ar, zh.
- RTL support for Arabic: auto-flip layout.

### Output Required

Generate localisation architecture, screen behaviour, and UI interaction flow for multilingual switching.

**Developing Multilingual Support**

Okay, so I'm finally moving forward with this multilingual support for the NutriForge app. The key is in those first few steps. I've been focusing on adding a language selection screen right into onboarding, which looks like a good starting point. Next, I am thinking about how to get that selected language stored globally. And then I have to think about that translation dictionary.


**Adding More Languages**

I am now focusing on implementing the language selection in the settings view, which is the next logical step. I've also added the `language` field to `UserProfile` and created the `i18n.ts` file to hold string translations. I am also working on passing the `language` state down through the app and making sure that the views utilize a translation helper function, which will be called `t()`, to fetch UI strings. I will next focus on RTL layout support for Arabic and ensuring AI services receive the user's language setting.


**Implementing Text Translations**

Okay, I've got a lot done today. I've updated the `views/Insights.tsx` and `views/FreeMode.tsx` to use the `t()` function and made the needed changes in `services/geminiService.ts` to request responses in the user's preferred language. Next, I need to focus on implementing the RTL layout for Arabic. I will add that `dir` attribute to the main app container. I will add the necessary code in `i18n.ts` for English, Hindi, Chinese, and Arabic.

payload.text:
# 🥗 GOQii NutriForge – Home Page UI/UX Prompt

## App Module
GOQii NutriForge — AI Powered Nutrition Intelligence

## Objective
Design a powerful nutrition home dashboard that lets users manage:
• Daily meals  
• Weekly planning  
• Grocery list  
• Nutrition targets  
• Trending meal plans  
• Recipes & wellness blogs  

The home page must instantly answer:
- What should I eat today?
- How am I tracking against my nutrition goals?
- What can I explore next?

---

## 🧠 SCREEN STRUCTURE

### 1. TOP HEADER
- Greeting with user name  
- Date  
- Subtext: *Your personalised nutrition plan for today*

---

### 2. NUTRITION TARGETS SNAPSHOT

Show progress rings / bars:

| Metric | UI |
|------|----|
| Calories | Ring – Consumed vs Target |
| Protein | Progress Bar |
| Carbs | Progress Bar |
| Fat | Progress Bar |

CTA: **View Nutrition Targets**

---

### 3. TODAY’S MEALS

Vertical meal cards for:
- Breakfast  
- Lunch  
- Snack  
- Dinner  

Each card contains:
- Meal image  
- Meal name  
- Calories  
- Status badge: Logged / Not Logged  
- Actions:
  - **Log Meal**
  - **Generate Alternative**

---

### 4. TRENDING NUTRITION PLANS

Horizontal scroll cards:
- Fat Loss Reset – 7 Days  
- Heart Smart – 7 Days  
- Muscle Builder – 7 Days  
- Indian Weight Loss – 7 Days  

CTA: **View All Plans**

---

### 5. TRENDING RECIPES

Horizontal carousel:
- Recipe image  
- Calories  
- Prep time  
- Save icon  

CTA: **Browse Recipes**

---

### 6. QUICK ACTIONS STRIP

Icon buttons:
- Weekly Planner  
- Grocery List  
- Nutrition Targets  
- Meal History  

---

### 7. WEEKLY PLANNER PREVIEW

Mini calendar:
- Today highlighted  
- Tap a day to view meals  

CTA: **Open Weekly Planner**

---

### 8. SMART AI TIPS

Rotating insight card:
- *You’re low on protein today.*  
- *Swap white rice for brown rice at lunch.*

---

### 9. BLOGS & WELLNESS CONTENT

Title: **From the GOQii Health Desk**

Blog cards:
- Blog image  
- Title  
- Read time  

CTA: **Read More**

---

## 🎨 DESIGN STYLE

- Light theme  
- GOQii green accent color  
- Rounded cards  
- Clean healthcare typography  
- Soft gradients  
- Smooth progress animations  

---

## 🔄 INTERACTIONS

- Logging a meal updates nutrition targets instantly  
- Generate Alternative opens food swap suggestions  
- Progress bars animate on update  
- Weekly planner slides up from bottom  

---

## OUTPUT REQUIRED
Generate full UI layout, components, and navigation logic for this NutriForge Home Page.

**Considering Language Integration**

I'm currently focused on integrating global language selection into the GOQii NutriForge onboarding process. My plan involves modifying `views/Onboarding.tsx` to include a UI element for language selection, possibly leveraging `components/UI.tsx` for consistency. I'll need to update `types.ts` to accommodate the language selection data, and also consider how this impacts `services/geminiService.ts` for localized content. I am now exploring possible internationalization libraries.


**Implementing Global Language Support**

I'm now fully immersed in global language support. The previous work was incomplete, so I'm now crafting a comprehensive solution. I'm focusing on adding language selection during onboarding, and ensuring the user can change this setting later. I'm also addressing RTL support for Arabic and plan on updating the AI prompts to accommodate the chosen language. I'm working on `types.ts`, `i18n.ts`, and `App.tsx` for state management, while addressing other supporting files.


**Orchestrating Language Implementation**

I'm now fully immersed in implementing the complete language management system. I'm focusing on managing language state and handling RTL support. Onboarding will start with language selection, with all screens translating accordingly. I'm updating `views/Onboarding.tsx`, `views/Settings.tsx`, `services/geminiService.ts`, and other key views. I'm also preparing to test the new visual appearance, including the flag icons and consistent GOQii branding.



**Refining Language Integration**

I'm now fully immersed in refining the language integration. I've updated `UserProfile`, created `i18n.ts`, and updated `App.tsx` for state management and translation functionality. I've added language options to `views/Onboarding.tsx` and `views/Settings.tsx`, and I'm currently localizing the `Dashboard` and `Insights` screens, including RTL support where needed. I'm also localizing `PlanSelection.tsx` and `FreeMode.tsx`, and updating `services/geminiService.ts` with localized prompts.

To satisfy your request, I will implement a robust internationalization (i18n) system for **GOQii NutriForge**. This includes a new language selection step at the very beginning of the onboarding process, a translation dictionary for English, Hindi, Chinese, and Arabic, and full Right-to-Left (RTL) support for the Arabic interface.

### Specification

1.  **I18n Architecture**:
    *   Created a new `i18n.ts` dictionary containing localized strings for all UI elements.
    *   Supported languages: English, Hindi, Chinese (Simplified), and Arabic.
    *   Added a global `t(key)` helper in `App.tsx` passed down to all views.
2.  **Global Language State**:
    *   Language is now part of the `UserProfile` and persistent across the session.
    *   Changing language in Settings instantly updates the entire UI and layout direction.
3.  **Onboarding Updates**:
    *   **Step 0 (Language)**: Users now see a beautiful language selection screen before seeing any other content.
    *   All subsequent onboarding questions are translated based on the initial choice.
4.  **Visual and UX Enhancements**:
    *   **RTL Support**: When Arabic is selected, the layout flips (status bar icons, navigation, text alignment, and "back" arrows) using the `dir="rtl"` attribute.
    *   **Settings Integration**: A "Language" section in Settings allows users to switch their preference anytime with a single tap.
    *   **AI Context**: The Gemini API prompts now strictly instruct the model to respond in the user's chosen language.

To check your Gemini API key:

1.  **Google AI Studio Dashboard**: Visit [aistudio.google.com/app/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey) to view your existing keys, check their status, or create new ones.
2.  **Application Console**: Open your browser's Developer Tools (F12) and check the **Console** tab. If the key is invalid or restricted, you will see `401 (Unauthorized)` or `403 (Forbidden)` errors when the app tries to "Forge" a plan or recipe.
3.  **Environment Variable**: In this project, the key is automatically injected via `process.env.API_KEY`. You do not need to (and should not) add any UI elements to enter or display the key within the app itself.
